To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LTA is the Gram-positive endotoxic molecule that elicits a proinflammatory response in human blood similar to that of LPS.
lipoteichoic acids (LTAs) and lipopeptides induce the activation of murine macrophages and human blood neutrophils, respectively.

LTA is a potent proinflammatory molecule in human blood, but not in murine macrophae, whereas lipoteichoic acids and lipopeptides are potent immunostimulants in both murine macrophages and human blood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the Gram-positive bacterial endotoxins and their role in the pathogenesis, as well as in the prevention, of Gram-positive sepsis.
the characterization of the immunostimulation and inflammatory mediator production by the Gram-positive bacterial endotoxin, lipoteicho acid, in comparison to the Gram-negative endotoxin, LPS.
the development of a new class of anti-inflammatory agents for the treatment of sepsis and other inflammatory diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Gram-positive bacterial components LTA, PGN, and lipopeptide, are potent activators of innate immunity, but their immunostimulatory potency is lower than that of the Gram-negative bacterial endotoxin LPS.
, in the context of human blood, LTA and LPS are the Gram-positive and Gram-negative endotoxins that are the best suited to elicit a proinflammatory response.
, in the murine system, lipopeptides are potent NF-kappaB inducers, but weak cytokine inducers, whereas LTA is a potent cytokine inducer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipopeptides are potent agonists for murine macrophages, but their immunostimulatory activities in human blood are limited to the neutrophils, and they are considerably less potent than LTA.
LTA, PGN, and lipopeptide are not as potent as LPS in their immunostimulatory or proinflammatory activities in either murine or human cells.
the TLR2/6 ligand, diacyl lipopeptides, is the most potent immunostimulatory ligand, whereas the LTA/TLR2 ligand is the most proinflammatory ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gram-positive endo- and exotoxins are not equivalent in terms of their immunostimulation and cytokine-inducing activities.
, while the lipoteichoic acids are potent TLR2 agonists, their immunostimulatory activity in human blood is significantly lower than that of the LPS.
the lipopeptides and LTA are not likely candidates for the Gram-positive endogenous ligand for TLR2.
